prompt: What is effective demand?

options.label: A
options.text: The desire to own a product even when the consumer cannot pay

options.label: B
options.text: The quantity bought only when the price is zero

options.label: C
options.text: The willingness and ability to buy a product at a given price

options.label: D
options.text: The amount producers wish to sell at a given price

explanation: Demand is effective when a buyer both wants the product and has the purchasing power to buy it at the stated price. Desire alone does not create a market purchase.

options.label: C

options.label: D

prompt: What does a market demand curve show?

options.label: A
options.text: The amount consumers want regardless of ability to pay

options.label: B
options.text: The quantity one consumer buys at one price

options.label: C
options.text: The total quantity firms are willing and able to offer for sale at each price in a specified period

options.label: D
options.text: The total quantity consumers are willing and able to buy at different prices

explanation: A market demand curve combines all buyers’ quantities at each price, holding other determinants constant. It therefore shows total willingness and ability to buy, not one buyer’s purchases or firms’ sales plans.
reference: 2.1 Demand and supply curves | 2.1.2 individual and market demand and supply | AO1 Knowledge and Understanding

prompt: What does a market supply curve show?

options.label: A
options.text: The maximum productive capacity of all firms

options.label: B
options.text: The total quantity firms are willing and able to sell at different prices

options.label: C
options.text: The total quantity consumers are willing and able to buy at each price during a specified period

options.label: D
options.text: The quantity one firm produces at one price

explanation: The market supply curve records the quantities all sellers are willing and able to offer at alternative prices. Productive capacity alone does not show how much firms would actually offer at each price.
reference: 2.1 Demand and supply curves | 2.1.2 individual and market demand and supply | AO1 Knowledge and Understanding

prompt: How is a market demand curve obtained from individual demand curves?

options.label: B
options.text: By adding quantities demanded horizontally at each price

options.label: C
options.text: By selecting the demand of the largest consumer

options.label: D

prompt: How is a market supply curve obtained from individual firms’ supply curves?

options.text: By selecting the supply of the largest firm

options.text: By adding firms’ prices at each quantity
